originality.rationale: Sakagawa arXiv:2610.00901v1 Proposition 1.1 covers the finite stationary product law, Theorem 2.3 a general two-coordinate local limit theorem, and Lemma 2.4 only coarse saturated-debt concentration at fixed transfer laws. This is partly covering background, especially the q=1 endpoint. The present claim instead establishes a triangular family of asymmetry parameters with a_N log(g_-/g_+) converging to an arbitrary finite drift, an intermediate bias regime, and an order-one geometric endpoint, with explicit means and one uniform combinatorial proof. Direct semantic comparisons found no matching three-regime microscopic slack theorem. Lack of a published statement is not uniqueness proof. A broad general conditioning theorem might subsume the result; this is the principal remaining priority risk.
residual_risks: The broad Sakagawa local limit theorem, specialized to q=1, may imply the balanced exponential endpoint with a short extra argument; do not interpret that endpoint as independently novel.
An unlocated general local equivalence-of-ensembles or tilted-partition theorem could imply the full triangular critical bias and saturation classification.
Predecessor full-text access was less complete than inspection of the focal source; published-equivalence priority requires independent review.

value.rationale: Unused common-bank credit is a natural finite-system observable invisible to macroscopic one-site wealth marginals. The result identifies an actual sharp noncommuting-transition scale in an exchange mechanism: O(a_N) slack at balanced rates, O(1/log q_N) at vanishing but stronger bias, and O(1) geometric slack at fixed rate skew. The explicit critical exponential parameter quantifies saturation and can guide simulations and high-temperature asymptotics, rather than constituting a purely cosmetic reparameterization.
